description: ASTROZO is a team of four female students from Al-Balqa Applied University, Jordan, studying Software Engineering and Data Science. Our project, AstroKids, is an interactive game that teaches children astronaut skills through space missions and challenges. We love technology, creativity, and space exploration. We welcome teammates skilled in web development, game design, UI/UX, animation, or scientific research!
summary: ASTROZO turns NASA’s open data into an interactive journey that anyone can explore, no science background required. We built a [web app / mobile app] that takes complex space and Earth-observation datasets and transforms them into clear visuals, live insights, and short guided stories. Our solution addresses the challenge by making NASA data accessible, understandable, and actionable for students, educators, and curious minds worldwide. It matters because data is only powerful when people can understand it. ASTROZO closes the gap between raw scientific data and public curiosity, inspiring the next generation to explore, question, and protect our planet and beyond. With a simple interface, engaging visuals, and a scalable design, ASTROZO brings space to everyone’s screen.
details:
What it does: ASTROZO connects to NASA open datasets and converts them into interactive maps, charts, and animated visual stories. Users choose a topic, explore real data, and see what it means in simple language.

How it works: The app collects data from NASA sources, processes it, and presents it through an intuitive interface with visual layers and short explanations. Users can compare, zoom, and discover patterns on their own.

Benefits:

  • Makes NASA data understandable for everyone, from students to the general public.
  • Encourages learning through exploration, not memorization.
  • Works as a ready-to-use educational tool for classrooms and communities.

Intended impact: We want to spark curiosity about space and Earth science, build data literacy, and help people see how NASA’s open data connects to real life.
